speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when you first noticed the swelling and pain in your right ring finger, and did any injury or bite precede it?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any immediate bruising or deformity at the time of the injury, and are you currently able to bend the finger at all? Does the pain worsen when you try to straighten it?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if you could actively extend the finger before this injury, and can you feel any clicking sensation when you try to make a fist? Also, have you noticed any skin discoloration or a visible lump at the tip of the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the mechanism of injury and your inability to flex the distal joint, I suspect a mallet finger. To confirm the extent of the damage, I need to see the joint's alignment. REQUEST TEST: Right Ring Finger X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms there are no fractures, which points to a soft tissue injury like a tendon rupture. Can you try to actively straighten your finger using only your own strength, or does it only straighten when I manually lift it? This will help determine if the extensor tendon is completely torn.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you can't actively extend the tip and the X-ray shows no fracture, I suspect a tendon avulsion. Can you confirm if the finger droops downward when you relax your hand, or does it stay straight on its own?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your response about denying fever and numbness is noted, but it doesn't answer my previous question about the finger's resting position. Does the tip of your ring finger droop downward when you relax your hand, or does it stay straight on its own?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Dr. Agent: You mentioned earlier that your finger is extended in the resting position, which is unusual for a typical mallet finger where the tip usually droops. Can you clarify if you are currently unable to actively bend the tip of your finger downward at all, even when you try to make a fist?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right Ring Finger Clinical Photo

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Patient, I am concerned because you are unable to actively bend the tip of your ring finger, which suggests a disruption of the flexor tendon rather than the extensor. Since you denied numbness, can you confirm if you have any sensation of "triggering" or catching when you try to move the finger? This is my ninth question.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Flexor Digitorum Profundus Tendon Avulsion (Jersey Finger) of the right ring finger.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
